title: Contains Duplicate
prompt: Given an integer list nums, return True if any value appears at least twice, and False if every element is distinct. Implement `def contains_duplicate(nums: list[int]) -> bool`.

title: Valid Anagram
prompt: Given two strings s and t, return True if t is an anagram of s. Implement `def is_anagram(s: str, t: str) -> bool`.

title: Two Sum
prompt: Given a list of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Exactly one solution exists. Implement `def two_sum(nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]`.

title: Group Anagrams
prompt: Given a list of strings, group the anagrams together and return the groups in any order. Implement `def group_anagrams(strs: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]`.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
prompt: Given an integer list nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements in any order. Implement `def top_k_frequent(nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]`.

title: Valid Palindrome
prompt: Return True if string s is a palindrome after lowercasing it and removing all non-alphanumeric characters. Implement `def is_palindrome(s: str) -> bool`.

title: Container With Most Water
prompt: Given a list height where height[i] is the height of a vertical line at position i, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water. Return that maximum area. Implement `def max_area(height: list[int]) -> int`.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
prompt: Given a list prices where prices[i] is a stock price on day i, return the maximum profit from one buy followed by one later sell, or 0 if no profit is possible. Implement `def max_profit(prices: list[int]) -> int`.
reference:
def max_profit(prices: list[int]) -> int:
    lowest = float('inf')
    best = 0
    for p in prices:
        lowest = min(lowest, p)
        best = max(best, p - lowest)
    return best

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
prompt: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Implement `def length_of_longest_substring(s: str) -> int`.

title: Valid Parentheses
prompt: Given a string containing only the characters ()[]{}, return True if every bracket is closed by the same type in the correct order. Implement `def is_valid(s: str) -> bool`.

title: Binary Search
prompt: Given a sorted list of integers nums and a target, return the index of target or -1 if it is absent. The solution must run in O(log n). Implement `def search(nums: list[int], target: int) -> int`.

title: Reverse Linked List
prompt: Given the head of a singly linked list (class ListNode with attributes val and next), reverse the list and return the new head. Implement `def reverse_list(head: ListNode | None) -> ListNode | None`.

title: Invert Binary Tree
prompt: Given the root of a binary tree (class TreeNode with attributes val, left and right), invert the tree by swapping every left and right child, and return its root. Implement `def invert_tree(root: TreeNode | None) -> TreeNode | None`.

title: Number of Islands
prompt: Given a 2D grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), return the number of islands. An island is land connected horizontally or vertically. Implement `def num_islands(grid: list[list[str]]) -> int`.

title: Climbing Stairs
prompt: You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top of a staircase with n steps. Implement `def climb_stairs(n: int) -> int`.

title: Coin Change
prompt: Given a list of coin denominations and an amount, return the fewest coins needed to make the amount, or -1 if it cannot be made. Each coin may be used unlimited times. Implement `def coin_change(coins: list[int], amount: int) -> int`.

title: Subsets
prompt: Given a list of unique integers, return all possible subsets (the power set) in any order. Implement `def subsets(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]`.
reference:
def subsets(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    result = []
    path = []

    def backtrack(i: int) -> None:
        if i == len(nums):
            result.append(path.copy())
            return
        path.append(nums[i])
        backtrack(i + 1)
        path.pop()
        backtrack(i + 1)

    backtrack(0)
    return result

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
prompt: Given an integer list nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element. Implement `def find_kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int`.

title: Merge Intervals
prompt: Given a list of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the result. Implement `def merge(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]`.

title: Single Number
prompt: Every element of the non-empty integer list nums appears twice except for one. Return that single element using O(1) extra space. Implement `def single_number(nums: list[int]) -> int`.
